events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
The trip was RydeTAXI, metered, charged $40.62 with distance $26.71 for 18.9 km, time $7.50 for 28.8 min, waiting $1.04 and platform $1.47 [F8]. The only off-route segment is 12:24–12:35, 4.63 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.64 km [F4], and it must be tested segment by segment under RD-1/RD-3/RD-5.

The rider's own message, sent at 12:20 and timestamped before the segment began at 12:24, names the place: "Can you stop at Paya Lebar Square? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes" [F9][F11]. The driver accepted at 12:21 ("Ok") [F10]. The car stopped at (1.3175, 103.8922) for 4 min 0 s, 12:28–12:32 [F2], i.e. inside the segment window.

Under RD-3(a), where the rider names a specific place and the car stops there, the whole way to that place is not a detour; its extra km are exempt in full, regardless of how far the place was or how long the stop lasted. The named place is the new destination for that stretch [RD-1][RD-3].

The RD-4 screen fails: there is no qualifying traffic incident on the replaced optimal stretch during the trip window [F15]; the speed-band records on PIE and CTE are band 4 (30–39 km/h), which is neither band 1 nor 2 and in any case only corroborates an incident, it does not exempt alone [F13][F14][RD-4].

Because the single off-route segment is exempt under RD-3, there is no unexempted detour segment and the RD-2 refund is Σ(exempt) × rate = 0 km × $1.4102/km = $0.00 [F4][F8][RD-2]. The fare excess of $4.89 (3.5 km × $1.41/km) is the mileage of that same exempt stretch and is therefore not refundable [F5].

The waiting charge of $1.04 for 4.0 min at $0.26/min [F6] is the RydeTAXI meter's waiting unit and is collectible under RD-3(c); the 4 min stop the rider requested does not make it refundable [F2][F6][RD-3]. No app-based destination change fee appears in the fare breakdown [F8].

RD-6 is not triggered: the driver has 1 upheld dispute in 90 d but route_disputes_upheld_90d is 0, so this is not a repeated route breach and no account flag is called for [F18][RD-6]. The rider's profile (2 disputes in 90 d, 0 upheld) does not decide anything [F17].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement [F9][F10][F12]. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the complaint disputes only money and clearly accepts the Paya Lebar Square stop was made ("we did, fine") [F9]. Nothing to escalate under SAFE-1 or SAFE-2.

The rider's real complaint is that the metered fare exceeded a 15.5 km estimate; on a metered taxi the meter, not the estimate, is the fare, and the only deviation in the record was rider-requested [F1][F3][F8][F9]. The outcome is therefore no_action.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We looked into your Paya Lebar Square complaint and no refund is due. You asked in the app to stop there for a parcel, and the driver agreed, so that stretch of the trip doesn't count as a detour — the extra distance isn't refundable. The amount you paid was the meter fare (a distance charge, a time charge, a waiting charge for the 4 minutes you were stopped, and a platform fee), and the waiting charge stands. Nothing changes on your account, and no further action will be taken on this complaint.

DRIVER: We reviewed the Paya Lebar Square complaint and found no issue with your trip, so no action is being taken against you. The records show the rider asked you in the app to stop there and you agreed before the detour began, and the car did stop there — so that stretch is treated as a rider-requested stop, not an unauthorised detour. The waiting charge for the stop is collectible, and no fare is being deducted from you. Your account is unaffected; this won't be counted against you.
